correctness.rationale: Exact scaling and parity dissection give finite-n distributional identities. A centered symmetric Taylor expansion proves the uniform gamma(gamma-1)/2 coefficient and local variance gamma^2(gamma-1)^2/720 times offset^(2gamma-4), with controlled remainder. Below 3/2 the variance sum converges, giving independent L2 series and non-Gaussianity by Cramér; at gamma=1 there is exact even zero versus odd uniform error. At and above 3/2 the harmonic/power variance divergences and bounded-summand Lindeberg yield the asserted CLTs and exact constants 1/640 and c_gamma. Verified by 356 deterministic finite checks in verify.py; finite checks are not treated as infinite proof. Ranges and exceptional gamma=1,2 were checked.

originality.rationale: The claim is a joint limit-law and grid-phase classification for a centered interior cusp, not a variance-rate estimate. Wu introduces exactly the local complementary-pair algorithm and proves unbiasedness plus Sobolev error bounds, but does not provide distributional cusp laws. Endpoint-power second-moment asymptotics alone do not yield the odd central-cell law or distributional limits. The examined Gaussian-weight trapezoid and generalized Latin-hypercube CLT concern different algorithms or asymptotic parameters. Classical independent-array CLT and normal decomposition are explicitly treated as standard inputs. Remaining risk: an unlocated equivalent theorem for local antithetic stratification may exist.
residual_risks: An unlocated prior specialization of antithetic triangular-array limit theory may reproduce some or all cusp-phase distributional laws under different terminology.
The result is for a rational cusp phase of exactly one half, not all interior shifts; cannot claim generality or global literature uniqueness.

value.rationale: Distributional error laws determine how stochastic quadrature uncertainty behaves, unlike variance rates alone. The cusp changes the effective number of influential strata: summable variance yields a non-Gaussian local error series, critical harmonic accumulation yields a logarithmic CLT, and square-summable curvature away from the cusp yields the Gaussian n^(-5/2) regime. Exact parity at gamma=1 shows a strong, useful grid-placement obstruction for a standard integration test. Natural full parameter classification with explicit constants and precise limitations; no unsupported wider implications.
